title: Test plan draft
description: What the Planner sub-agent hands back. The orchestrator normalizes an accepted draft into a test-plan document. Prose is the human contract; the optional assert is the machine-checkable predicate the generated test evaluates.

notes.description: One or two sentences on how the plan was scoped.

openQuestions.description: What could not be determined from the site map. Prefer saying so over inventing page text.

id.description: Stable snake or kebab id, e.g. checkout_happy_path.

rationale.description: Why this flow is worth testing on THIS application.

preconditions.description: Use "authenticated" when the flow requires a signed-in session.

requirementIds.description: PRD requirement ids this flow covers. Omit or leave empty when it covers none.

intent.description: What the user is trying to do, in their words.

page.description: Path this step happens on, e.g. /checkout.

inputs.description: Field values this step supplies, using the exact input name from the site map.

expect.description: Omit on a pure action step; the orchestrator folds it into the step that asserts its outcome.

prose.description: The human-readable expectation, e.g. "Order confirmation is visible".

predicate.description: Never copy the prose into value. The value must be text observed in the crawl, not a description of it.

value.description: Literal string expected in the page, or the URL fragment.
